conceptCapsule.title: Linear Acceleration in Pure Rolling on an Incline
conceptCapsule.summary: When a symmetric body rolls down an incline of angle $\theta$ without slipping, static friction prevents slipping at the contact point ($v_{\text{contact}} = 0$) without dissipating mechanical energy.
conceptCapsule.examTrap: The acceleration $a_{\text{cm}}$ is independent of total mass $M$ and radius $R$.

questions.statement: A solid cylinder of mass $M$ and radius $R$ rolls down an incline of angle $\theta$ without slipping. Find the magnitude of the friction force acting on it.
questions.solution:
1. Linear acceleration: $$a = \frac{g \sin\theta}{1 + I/MR^2} = \frac{2}{3}g \sin\theta$$
2. Torque about center of mass: $$f R = I \alpha = \left(\frac{1}{2}MR^2\right)\left(\frac{a}{R}\right)$$
3. Yields friction force: $$f = \frac{1}{3}Mg \sin\theta$$
